It is reported that Apple is preparing to unveil its first foldable iPhone on September 9. Bloomberg, citing an IDC report, is optimistic about the device's first-year sales performance. Details below.

IDC Optimistic on First-Year Shipments for iPhone Ultra

At next month's 'Surprise and shine' event, Apple is widely expected to announce its first book-style foldable iPhone, with market rumours pointing to a price of around US$2,500.

Despite years of market scepticism about the category, Counterpoint Research recently forecast that book-style devices will account for 76% of global foldable smartphone shipments in 2026, up from 52% in 2025, with Apple's entry into the fray driving overall market growth of 21% year-on-year.

Now, IDC (via Bloomberg) is equally upbeat on Apple首款 foldable iPhone's projected first-year shipments after launch.

Bloomberg reported, citing IDC senior research director Nabila Popal, that Apple is expected to 'ship over 10 million units in the first year', despite the premium pricing.

For reference, Samsung's newly launched Galaxy Z Fold 8, which uses a passport-like aspect ratio—a design Apple's foldable iPhone is also rumoured to adopt—starts at US$1,899 for the 256GB storage with 12GB RAM version.

A recent Counterpoint Research report noted that Samsung led the foldable smartphone market with a 40% share in 2025, but its share is projected to drop to 32% in 2026, while Apple is estimated to account for 25% of shipments in 2026 alone.

Notably, Counterpoint's forecast covers only the full year of 2026, while IDC's projection of over 10 million shipments spans the entire first year following the foldable iPhone's launch.

That said, both reports are optimistic about the iPhone Ultra's performance.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that Apple's entry into the foldable market would help 'avoid a double-digit percentage decline in foldable devices this year', adding that the category 'will grow 12.6% this year and accelerate to 18% next year'.

IDC also predicted that Apple will 'ultimately account for 40% of all foldable device shipments in 2027'.
